idea: Why to-do lists make you less productive
text:
I used to think a longer list meant more control.

I see my brain stall when I scan ten items. Each choice eats energy before I start. I notice I pick the easiest task just to cross something off. Try picking one priority tonight. If you feel stuck tomorrow, cut the list to three items and watch your pace shift.

I spend time rewriting instead of doing. I used to copy tasks into apps for neatness. That extra loop delays real work and builds stress. Leave tasks where they land. If you catch yourself recopying, stop and start the first action instead.

I feel done after checking boxes. I’ve seen myself celebrate a cleared list while the big project stayed untouched. The tick mark gives a fake win. Watch for that relief after a check. If it happens, move straight to the hardest step without adding more.

I prefer one clear focus over a stack of marks.
title: Why to-do lists make you less productive
